high.title: Dollar-Won Takes Breather on Softer PCE, Closes at 1,543.10 Won
high.summary:
The USD/KRW exchange rate edged marginally higher in overnight New York trading, closing at 1,543.10 won — up just 1.30 won from the previous Seoul session close. The modest move came despite the U.S. dollar index retreating for the first time in four consecutive sessions, as softer-than-expected PCE inflation data weighed on the greenback. Two key technical factors capped the upside on USD/KRW: (1) exporter dollar supply pressure tied to month-end and half-year-end settlement flows, a predictable seasonal dynamic that typically sees Korean exporters repatriating foreign earnings; and (2) easing inflation prints reducing near-term Fed hawkishness expectations. For KRW traders, the 1,543 level represents a critical near-term anchor. The confluence of softer U.S. inflation and exporter supply suggests downside pressure on USD/KRW could build heading into month-end. Watch for whether Seoul's opening session on the 26th sees continued exporter-driven KRW strength, and monitor whether the PCE data shifts BOK rate cut expectations further into view.

---

high.title: US Core PCE Price Index Rises 0.3% MoM in May, Maintaining Moderate Pace (Comprehensive)
high.summary:
The US core PCE price index — the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge — rose 0.3% month-on-month in May, in line with market expectations and maintaining a moderate trajectory. Headline PCE came in at 0.4% MoM. For KRW/USD traders, this is a critical data point: a benign core PCE reading reduces the probability of a near-term Fed rate hike, which generally limits USD upside and offers some relief to EM currencies including the Korean Won. If the Fed interprets this as confirmation that inflation is on a sustainable downward path, it could accelerate expectations for rate cuts, potentially tightening the US-Korea rate differential and supporting KRW. Korean government bond (KTB) markets may also benefit from a softer rate outlook, as reduced Fed hawkishness tends to anchor long-end yields globally. Traders should watch upcoming FOMC communications closely to assess whether this reading shifts the dot plot or rate cut timeline, which will be the primary near-term driver of USD/KRW direction.

---

high.title: Foreigners Snap Up Bonds Amid Sharp Market Correction - 3-Year Treasury Yield Falls 3.5bp
high.summary: South Korean government bond yields fell sharply on June 26th, with the move concentrated in short- to medium-term maturities as investors rotated out of equities into safe-haven fixed income. The benchmark 3-year Korean Treasury Bond (KTB) yield declined 3.5 basis points, reflecting a classic risk-off repositioning. Notably, a late-session plunge in the dollar-won exchange rate — attributed by market participants to suspected official intervention by Korean authorities — provided additional tailwind to the bond rally. Foreign investors were active buyers during the session, reinforcing the bullish tone. However, ultra-long bond yields bucked the trend and rose, driven by supply concerns ahead of an upcoming auction. **Key implications:** The suspected FX intervention signals that authorities remain sensitive to won strength reaching certain thresholds. Foreign buying of KTBs amid equity weakness suggests continued appetite for Korean duration as a regional safe-haven. Watch for further auction dynamics at the long end and any BOK commentary on FX intervention. The interplay between equity corrections and bond inflows is a critical theme for portfolio positioning.

high.title: IRS Rates Plunge in Short to Medium Terms on Stock Correction and Won Strength
high.summary: Interest rate swap (IRS) rates fell sharply across the short-to-medium curve on June 26th, with the 1-year IRS down 3.75 basis points to 3.4550%, while the 3-year and 5-year tenors dropped 5.50bp and 5.25bp respectively as of the 4:27 p.m. close. Market participants cited two primary drivers: heightened safe-haven demand following a sharp equity market correction, and bullish sentiment stemming from the declining dollar-won exchange rate. The won's appreciation — likely amplified by suspected official intervention — effectively compressed rate expectations at the front and belly of the swap curve. **Key implications for fund managers:** The magnitude of the IRS move (5.5bp in the 3-year) is significant and suggests the market is pricing in a more accommodative rate outlook in response to the equity selloff. For KRW rates traders, the flattening pressure on the IRS curve warrants close attention. If equity weakness persists, further IRS compression is plausible. The alignment between spot FX moves and rate market dynamics underscores the tight cross-asset linkages in Korean markets currently.

high.title: [FX Close] Won Plunges 10.70 Won on Suspected Authorities' Intervention
high.summary: The dollar-won exchange rate closed at 1,532.00 won as of 3:30 p.m. on June 26 in the Seoul foreign exchange market, down 10.70 won from the previous session — marking the first decline in five consecutive trading days. The session opened notably higher at 1,547.30 won (+4.60 won from prior close), suggesting continued underlying dollar demand and upward pressure on USD/KRW early in the day. However, a wave of dollar-selling flows — widely presumed to be direct intervention by Korean FX authorities — flooded the market and drove the sharp reversal.

high.title: Key implications for KRW traders and bond investors:
Busan Bank Sees Dollar-Won Overshooting Gradually Easing in H2, Forecasts 1,490 Won in Q4
high.summary:
BNK Busan Bank has published a second-half KRW/USD outlook, projecting the dollar-won rate to gradually decline toward 1,490 won by Q4 2026. The bank identifies several won-positive catalysts: robust semiconductor export performance — a critical driver of Korea's current account surplus — and a narrowing Korea-U.S. interest rate differential as the Fed's easing cycle progresses. This combination is expected to ease the structural overshooting pressure that has weighed on KRW in recent quarters.

However, the bank flags key risks that could delay or derail the anticipated won strengthening. Middle East geopolitical tensions remain a wildcard for global risk appetite, while foreign capital flows — both equity and bond — will be critical to watch. Fed policy timing remains the dominant external variable; any hawkish repricing of U.S. rates could quickly reverse the narrowing differential thesis.

**For traders:** The 1,490 Q4 target implies meaningful KRW appreciation from current levels, suggesting a directional bias toward long KRW positions on dips. Monitor semiconductor export data and Fed communication closely as leading indicators for timing entries.

high.title: KTB Competitive Auctions Expected at 16–17 Trillion Won in Aug–Sept; Share of 2–3 Year Notes to Increase
high.summary:
Korea Treasury Bond (KTB) issuance volumes, which were deliberately curtailed in response to elevated interest rate volatility earlier in the year, are forecast to normalize progressively through Q3 2026. Competitive auction volumes for August and September are expected to rise to 16–17 trillion won (approximately $13.5–14.4 billion), a meaningful step-up from recent suppressed levels. Critically, the composition is expected to shift toward shorter-duration 2–3 year notes at the expense of ultra-long-term bonds.

**Market implications:** The tilt toward the short-to-mid belly of the curve is significant for bond investors. It suggests the government is either responding to tepid ultra-long demand or strategically managing duration supply to avoid further yield curve steepening. For KRW bond traders, watch for technical pressure on 2–3 year KTB yields as supply increases — this could widen the spread differential with longer tenors. Foreign investors holding duration-heavy KTB positions should reassess convexity risk given the supply normalization trajectory. The timing of this normalization also intersects with BOK rate cut expectations; any dovish pivot would support demand absorption at the short end.

high.title: Falling Oil Prices Ease Inflation Pressure - Weak Dollar May Return as Fed Rate Hike Concerns Subside
high.summary: A key forecast from Woori Bank economist Min Kyung-won suggests that a weaker USD environment — similar to what was observed earlier this year — could reemerge in H2 2026, driven by easing inflationary pressure stemming from declining international oil prices. Lower oil prices reduce cost-push inflation globally, which in turn diminishes the probability of additional Federal Reserve rate hikes. As Fed tightening concerns recede, the broad dollar index faces downward pressure, creating a more favorable backdrop for EM currencies including the KRW. The analyst specifically cites South Korea's solid economic fundamentals as a key support factor, suggesting the USD/KRW rate has room to stabilize and grind lower through the second half of the year. For KRW traders, this is a constructive signal — a sustained move below 1,530 becomes more plausible if the Fed remains on hold and oil stays soft. Bond investors should also note that easing inflation reduces pressure on the BOK to maintain a restrictive stance, which could support duration. Watch upcoming US CPI prints and BOK guidance closely.

high.title: Dollar-Won Pares Losses on Risk-Off Sentiment, Closes at 1,535.80 Won
high.summary: The USD/KRW overnight session delivered a nuanced picture: the rate initially moved lower but subsequently pared gains as risk-off sentiment swept through markets following a technology-led selloff in US equities. The dollar index recovered a meaningful portion of its intraday decline, pulling USD/KRW back up with it. The pair ultimately closed the overnight session at 1,535.80 won, still down 6.90 won from the prior Seoul FX close of 1,532.00 won (note: the directional move implies the overnight reference point differs from intraday Seoul close — traders should reconcile with NDF data). The interplay between equity risk sentiment and dollar demand remains the dominant near-term driver. For KRW traders, this highlights a key vulnerability: even in an environment where fundamentals favor KRW strength, a tech-driven equity risk-off episode can swiftly reverse FX gains. The session underscores the importance of monitoring US equity market direction, particularly the Nasdaq, as a leading indicator for short-term USD/KRW moves. A sustained stabilization in US tech would be needed to allow KRW to hold and extend gains through the 1,530 handle.

medium.title: Chicago Fed President: 'Inflation Moving in Wrong Direction... Slight Improvement in Services Sector'
medium.summary: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee expressed concern on June 25th that U.S. inflation has "recently been moving in the wrong direction," noting that the Fed has remained above its 2% target for five consecutive years. Goolsbee flagged the services sector as particularly worrying, though acknowledged a slight improvement. His comments introduce a cautiously hawkish Fed narrative that could counterbalance the softer PCE print, potentially limiting USD weakness and placing a floor under USD/KRW near current levels. For Korean bond and FX traders, sustained Fed hawkishness would delay any convergence between BOK and Fed rate paths, keeping carry dynamics relatively unfavorable for KRW-denominated assets. This is a key variable to monitor heading into the next FOMC meeting.

medium.title: US 7-Year Treasury Auction Draws Solid Demand, Yield Meets Expectations
medium.summary: The U.S. Treasury's $44 billion 7-year note auction cleared at a yield of 4.260%, down 3.0 basis points from last month's 4.290%, signaling healthy demand for U.S. duration. The bid-to-cover ratio slipped marginally to 2.50x from 2.52x but still came in slightly above the recent average. Solid U.S. Treasury demand at lower yields is broadly supportive of a risk-on tone, which tends to benefit EM assets including Korean equities and the won. Lower U.S. yields also incrementally compress the Korea-U.S. rate differential, a factor BOK will weigh when assessing the timing of any domestic rate adjustments. Korean government bond (KTB) traders should note the directional signal from U.S. duration demand as a near-term constructive input.

medium.title: Audit Agency to Probe Regulators Over Leveraged ETF Boom
medium.summary:
South Korea's Board of Audit and Inspection (BAI) has launched a comprehensive audit of the Financial Services Commission (FSC) and Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) in response to growing investment risk concerns following recent market volatility. The probe focuses on the rapid mainstreaming of leveraged ETFs and other high-risk retail products, with concerns centring on excessive costs and potential mis-selling practices. For institutional investors, this development signals potential tightening of retail investment product regulations in Korea, which could dampen speculative retail flows that have amplified recent market swings. Regulatory tightening in the ETF space may also have secondary implications for liquidity dynamics in Korean equities and, by extension, foreign portfolio flows and KRW volatility. This is a story to monitor as regulatory outcomes could reshape the retail investor landscape in Korea.

---

medium.title: KOSPI Surges 5.42% to Close at 8,930 - SK Hynix Soars 13%
medium.summary: While individual equity moves generally fall outside the core scope of this briefing, the magnitude of today's KOSPI rally (+5.42% to 8,930) is macro-relevant and warrants monitoring. A single-session move of this scale typically signals a significant risk-on shift driven by either a macro catalyst (e.g., trade deal progress, BOK signal, or global risk appetite recovery) or a resolution of a key political/geopolitical overhang. SK Hynix's 13% surge suggests semiconductors led the charge, likely tied to global AI/chip demand sentiment. For KRW traders, a sharp equity rally of this magnitude often coincides with foreign equity inflows that provide near-term KRW appreciation pressure. Bond investors should watch for any crowding-out of safe-haven demand for KTBs. The article content is truncated, so the specific catalyst remains unconfirmed — **this is a key data gap to resolve before markets open.**

medium.title: President Lee Signals Supplementary Budget for GPU Procurement
medium.summary: President Lee Jae-myung has floated the possibility of a supplementary budget (추경) to accelerate mass procurement of GPUs as part of Korea's national AI infrastructure push. While framed as a technology initiative, any supplementary budget carries direct fiscal implications for Korean government bond supply. An additional issuance of KTBs to fund a supplementary budget would pressure yields upward at the margin, particularly at the short-to-mid end of the curve. The scale of the supplementary budget remains unspecified, making it premature to price in a material yield impact — but this is a headline to track closely. For KRW, expansionary fiscal policy could be mildly supportive of growth expectations but may also widen the fiscal deficit narrative, a modest headwind depending on global risk appetite. **Watch for National Assembly budget committee deliberations for sizing and timing.**

medium.title: FX Swap Points Rise on Month-End Won Demand
medium.summary: FX swap points edged higher across all tenors on June 26th, driven by month-end won funding demand. The 1-year swap point closed at -14.90 won (up 0.30 won from the open), the 6-month at -6.80 won (+0.20 won), and the 3-month at -2.80 won (+0.15 won). The 1-month tenor also firmed modestly. While swap points remain firmly in negative territory — reflecting the persistent structural cost of swapping dollars into won — the month-end uptick is a typical seasonal pattern as institutions cover short-term KRW funding needs at period close. For FX and cross-currency basis traders, the continued deeply negative swap points signal ongoing dollar funding premium and limited near-term reversal pressure. This dynamic is relevant for foreign investors hedging KRW exposure and for assessing the relative attractiveness of KTB carry trades on a fully hedged basis.

medium.title: Top 5 Banks' Loan-Deposit Rate Spread Holds Steady at 1.392%
medium.summary: The average loan-deposit rate spread at South Korea's five major banks (KB Kookmin, Shinhan, Hana, Woori, and NH Nonghyup) edged up just 0.004 percentage points month-on-month to 1.392 percentage points in May, based on new household loan volumes excluding policy-based inclusive finance, according to the Korea Federation of Banks. The spread's near-stability suggests limited immediate pressure on net interest margins (NIMs) at major lenders, and indicates that bank funding costs and lending rates are moving broadly in tandem. For macro watchers, a steady spread in the context of a potential BOK easing cycle is worth monitoring — if the BOK cuts policy rates further, banks may face margin compression unless lending rates hold firm. This data point is modestly relevant for assessing banking sector profitability and the transmission of monetary policy through the credit channel.

medium.title: Meritz Securities Issues 368 Billion Won Private Subordinated Bonds at 5.6%
medium.summary:
Meritz Securities issued 368 billion won (~$310 million) in private subordinated bonds on June 26 at a coupon rate of 5.60% per annum with a 30-year maturity. The bonds include a rate reset mechanism every five years, referencing a base rate plus spread with an additional 200 bps add-on, suggesting a step-up structure designed to incentivize early redemption. Meritz Fire & Marine Insurance is providing 70 billion won in affiliated support. This issuance is noteworthy as a credit market signal — the 5.60% coupon on long-dated subordinated financial paper provides a reference point for Korean financial sector credit spreads and reflects current funding cost conditions for non-bank financials. For bond investors, this pricing relative to KTB benchmarks offers a useful gauge of subordinated credit risk premium in the current rate environment.

---

medium.title: Financial Regulators Release Weekly Schedule — BOK Governor at BIS/ECB Forums; MPB Minutes Due
medium.summary: The BOK Governor will be on an international business trip June 29–30, attending the BIS Annual Conference, Board Meeting, and ECB Forum in Basel and Portugal respectively. Of direct market relevance: the minutes from the June 11th Monetary Policy Board meeting (a non-rate decision meeting) are scheduled for release on June 30 at 16:00 KST. These minutes could provide important color on the MPC's internal debate regarding the pace of future rate adjustments, inflation tolerance, and FX concerns. Bond and FX traders should parse the minutes for any dissenting views or shifts in the board's forward guidance language, which may reset expectations for the next rate decision.

medium.title: Ministry of Finance Weekly Schedule — July Individual Investment Government Bond Issuance Plan
medium.summary: The Ministry of Economy and Finance is set to release the July 2026 issuance plan for individual investment government bonds, alongside news of Korea's re-election to the WCO Policy Commission and Finance Committee. The retail bond issuance plan is a second-order indicator of the government's broader funding strategy and domestic demand cultivation efforts. While not a primary market mover, the July plan will provide incremental data on the government's appetite for retail distribution versus institutional auctions — relevant context for understanding overall KTB supply dynamics discussed in Article 3 above.

medium.title: NDF at 1,535.70/1,536.10 Won, Up 4.45 Won
medium.summary: The dollar-won one-month NDF rose in New York overnight trading, with the mid-rate quoted at 1,535.90 won. Accounting for the one-month swap point of -0.55 won, this implies an effective spot-equivalent level roughly 4.45 won higher than the previous Seoul FX close of 1,532.00 won. The bid/ask spread of 1,535.70 / 1,536.10 suggests orderly market conditions without significant liquidity stress. For FX traders, the NDF level signals mild upward pressure on the opening USD/KRW fix in Seoul, consistent with the risk-off tone described in overnight trading. The negative swap point continues to reflect Korea's interest rate differential dynamics relative to the US and warrants monitoring as BOK policy expectations evolve.

medium.title: Korea Treasury Futures Mixed Amid Oil Price Plunge - 10-Year Up 16 Ticks
medium.summary: Korean government bond futures posted a mixed performance in overnight trading, with the 3-year treasury futures unchanged at 103.29 while the 10-year futures gained 16 ticks to close at 107.14, indicating a bull-flattening bias at the long end. The divergence between short and long tenors is notable — the 3-year contract, more sensitive to BOK policy rate expectations, remained flat, while the 10-year contract benefited from the global disinflationary signal of plunging oil prices, which lowers long-term inflation expectations. Foreign investors were net sellers of 27 contracts in the 3-year space, while retail investors absorbed that selling — a flow dynamic worth tracking as it may suggest foreign accounts are cautious on near-term BOK easing. Bond investors with long duration positions in KTBs should view the oil-price-driven rally in the 10-year as a supportive but potentially fragile development, contingent on sustained oil weakness and softer global inflation data.

medium.title: S&P Affirms US Credit Rating at 'AA+' with Stable Outlook
medium.summary:
S&P has reaffirmed the United States' sovereign credit rating at 'AA+' with a 'stable' outlook, citing the resilience of the U.S. economy, sustained tariff revenues, and expectations of fiscal deficit stabilization over the coming years. While this is not a Korea-specific story, it carries indirect relevance for KRW/USD traders and Korean bond investors. A stable U.S. credit rating reduces near-term safe-haven demand volatility, which can support risk appetite in emerging market assets including Korean equities and KRW. Importantly, the affirmation removes a potential tail risk — a downgrade scenario that could have triggered a sharp USD rally and corresponding KRW depreciation pressure, similar to dynamics seen following the Moody's U.S. downgrade earlier in 2025. Fund managers should monitor whether this confirmation supports carry trade flows back into KRW-denominated assets and whether Korean government bond (KTB) yields see any modest downward pressure as global risk sentiment stabilizes. The reference to "sustained tariff income" suggests S&P views current U.S. trade policy as a fiscal tool rather than a systemic risk, which could temper concerns about global trade disruption impacting Korea's export-driven economy.
